Intelligent Research Assistant
Project Report
5
Security and Authentication
Security is paramount when handling proprietary research data. The system utilizes a
multi-layered security model.
5.1
JSON Web Tokens (JWT)
Authentication is stateless and managed via JSON Web Tokens. Upon successful login,
the backend issues an access_token signed with a strong, 256-bit secret key using the
HS256 algorithm.
The token payload contains the user’s unique ObjectId and an expiration timestamp.
The frontend stores this token in localStorage and attaches it to the Authorization:
Bearer <token> header of every subsequent HTTP request. The backend’s Depends(get_current_user
FastAPI dependency intercepts these requests, decodes the JWT, verifies the signature,
and rejects requests that are expired or tampered with.
5.2
Password Hashing
For users utilizing traditional email/password registration, passwords are never stored in
plaintext. The system uses the bcrypt hashing algorithm. Bcrypt inherently incorporates
a randomly generated "salt" for every password and relies on a tunable work factor (key
stretching) to make brute-force and rainbow-table attacks computationally infeasible.
5.3
Google OAuth & Firebase Integration
To reduce friction, the application implements OAuth2 login flows via Google Firebase.
By leveraging Firebase’s authentication SDKs, users can log in using their existing Google
accounts. The frontend intercepts the Firebase identity token and securely transmits it
to the Python backend, which verifies the token against Google’s public JWKS (JSON
Web Key Sets) before issuing a localized JWT.
